title: Beyond the forest of columns
dek: The Akhmenu changes the architectural language: tent-pole forms, royal ancestors and carved foreign plants.

sections.heading: A different building programme
paragraphs: The eastern Akhmenu belongs to Thutmose III’s transformation of Karnak. It is more than an extra room behind the earlier temple: its spaces bring together royal regeneration, divine worship and specialised cult settings. Sullivan cautions that its exact cultic character remains elusive.
This is a useful limit to carry while exploring. A convenient label such as “Festival Hall” helps orientation, but it does not explain every chamber’s function or every stage of use.

sections.heading: Columns with another model
paragraphs: The main hall’s unusual central columns are interpreted as stone versions of portable-tent supports. Compare the profile with the open-papyrus capitals in the Great Hypostyle Hall. The structural job is still to carry a roof, but the architectural form is different.

sections.heading: The botanical room is carved, not planted
paragraphs: The so-called botanical room lies in the northeastern part of the complex. Its reliefs show plants and animals associated with the king’s foreign campaigns. The modern nickname can mislead: what you study here is an architectural room and its images, not a surviving planted garden.

Begin with shapes and organisation. Notice a stem, branching leaves, or an isolated animal. A modern species name needs specialist botanical and epigraphic evidence. The guide should not turn resemblance into certainty.

sections.heading: The ancestors are elsewhere today
paragraphs: The Louvre records the Chambre des Ancêtres as originating in the Akhmenu and identifies it with inventory E 13481 BIS. Its reliefs show Thutmose III offering before royal predecessors. The original monument’s present collection context matters: a description of its ancient room must not promise that all its original carved walls remain in place at Karnak.
Treat the ancestor selection as a royal statement to interpret, rather than assume it is a complete neutral list of every king.
